question: What happens when the broker process gets SIGTERM during a deploy, and why does a graceful close matter?
answer_hinglish:
src/index.ts SIGINT aur SIGTERM dono par stop() chalata hai: ek stopping flag (double signal se dobara na chale), ek JSON log line jisme signal aur broker.stats() (connections, subscriptions, in/out counters, slowConsumers), phir broker.close(), phir doosri log line {event: 'stopped', how} jahan how 'closed' ya 'forced' hai, aur process.exit(0).

close(forceMs = 5000) graceful hai: pehle dialers ke timers band aur saare routes kaat diye jaate hain (cluster ho toh), phir server.close() se naye connections band, sab clients drop(c, false) -- routing band, subscriptions hatti, lekin socket destroy nahi -- phir har socket par end(). end() pehle se queued bytes bhejta hai aur PHIR FIN. Matlab jo messages close() se pehle accept ho chuke the, woh subscriber tak pahunchte hain. Test mein 500 messages queued the, close() ne 'closed' diya aur subscriber ko poore 500 mile.

Agar koi peer padhta nahi ya apni side kabhi band nahi karta (half-open), toh end() kabhi poora nahi hoga; isliye forceMs ke baad bache sockets destroy aur result 'forced'. Test allowHalfOpen wale socket se yeh dikhata hai.

Deploy ke liye kyun zaroori: har deploy ek shutdown hai. Stage 1 mein close() turant destroy karta tha, toh har deploy socket buffers mein pade messages giraata tha. Ab woh avoidable loss nahi hota. Cluster ho toh: route kat-te hi peers us broker ki interest hata dete hain, aur jin clients ke paas server list hai woh doosre broker par reconnect karke dobara subscribe karte hain (failover test). Jo abhi bhi hai: 'lame duck' mode nahi -- close() clients ko pehle se nahi batata ki doosre broker par jao; woh connection tootne par hi jaate hain, aur us beech ke publishes kahin nahi jaate.
why_needed: Agar shutdown har baar messages giraye, toh deploys hi data loss ka sabse bada source ban jaate hain.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant band karna: darwaza naye customers ke liye band, jo khaa rahe hain unhe khatam karne do, aur jo ghante bhar baithe rahein unhe ek tay waqt ke baad bahar.
how_it_works: SIGTERM -> stop(): log stats -> close(forceMs): server.close, drop(each, false), end() each socket -> all closed ? 'closed' : after forceMs destroy, 'forced' -> log 'stopped' -> exit(0).
in_this_project: src/index.ts stop handler; src/server.ts close(forceMs), drop. Tests test/stage2.test.ts 'graceful close' (500 messages delivered; half-open peer forced) aur server.test.ts 'close() drops every connection'.
advantages: Accepted messages deploy par nahi girte
Half-open peers shutdown nahi rokte (forceMs)
Log batata hai shutdown clean tha ya forced
disadvantages: Lame duck mode nahi: clients ko advance warning nahi
forceMs tak shutdown lamba ho sakta hai
common_mistakes: Shutdown par destroy() ko normal maan lena
Drain bina deadline ke (ek stubborn client shutdown rok dega)
Client ka drain() aur server ka graceful close ek samajhna

question: Why make the broker wire-compatible with the NATS client protocol instead of inventing a simpler protocol, and why zero runtime dependencies?
answer_hinglish:
Apna protocol banana aasaan lagta hai, lekin tab har test mera hi likha client chalayega, aur agar maine kuch galat samjha toh client aur server dono same galti karenge -- test phir bhi green. NATS ke client protocol ke saath wire-compatible hone se official nats npm client ek independent judge ban jaata hai. PLAN.md yahi decision likhta hai: official client sirf devDependency hai, tests mein use hota hai, aur jo hissa interoperate nahi karta woh likha jaata hai, chhupaya nahi.

Doosra fayda: protocol already sochi-samjhi hai -- byte-counted payloads, INFO mein max_payload, PING/PONG, -ERR, reply subjects. Mujhe framing aur error design dobara invent nahi karna pada, aur interview mein 'NATS jaisa' bolna concrete hai.

Keemat: compatibility ka scope sambhal kar bolna padta hai. Client protocol ka core hissa (stage 1 + 2: pub/sub, queue groups, headers, no responders) official client ke saath chalta hai, lekin auth fields abhi ignore hote hain, aur cluster protocol (src/route.ts) jaan-boojh kar apna hai, real NATS routes ke saath compatible nahi -- README aur route.ts ka header yahi kehte hain.

Zero runtime dependencies: server sirf node:net aur node:crypto (server_id ke randomBytes) use karta hai. Wajah: learning project hai, parser aur trie khud likhna hi point hai; supply-chain surface chhota; aur deploy par node_modules ka production install nahi. vitest, typescript aur nats sirf dev ke liye.
why_needed: Protocol choice decide karti hai ki aap apna kaam independently verify kar sakte ho ya nahi, aur dependencies security aur maintenance ka bojh hain.
real_world_analogy: Naya plug design karne ki jagah standard socket ke hisaab se appliance banao: kisi bhi ghar ki deewar mein lagao aur pata chal jayega kaam karta hai ya nahi.
how_it_works: Server INFO/MSG/-ERR NATS format mein likhta hai; official client connect, subscribe, publish, request karta hai; interop tests verify karte hain. package.json mein runtime dependencies nahi, sirf devDependencies.
in_this_project: src/server.ts imports sirf node:net aur node:crypto (aur local files); package.json devDependencies mein nats; test/interop.test.ts. PLAN.md 'Decisions' section.
advantages: Independent verification official client se
Proven protocol design reuse
Chhota supply-chain surface
disadvantages: Compatibility scope ko carefully bolna padta hai
Protocol ki har baat (jaise verbose, echo semantics) follow karni padti hai
Sab kuch khud likhna time leta hai
common_mistakes: 'Fully NATS compatible' claim karna jab auth nahi hai aur cluster protocol apna hai
Test-only library ko runtime dependency bana dena
Apne hi client se compatibility saabit karna
